notes: No kb/Work note owns either fix (none found). §1985:IX.4.6.2 prints REWRITE record-name-1 [ FROM identifier-1 ] [ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1 ] [ NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-2 ] [ END-REWRITE ]. The superset rule rewriteStatement accepts it, SequentialIoBinder.BindRewrite resolves record-name-1 and routes an indexed file to KeyedIoBinder.BindRewrite, and most of what the later formats add is refused at --std 85: FROM literal-1 and FROM a figurative constant by VisitRecordFromPhrase (COBOL0871), FILE file-name-1 by DeclinedFilePhrase (COBOL1706), RETRY by VisitRetryPhrase and WITH [NO] LOCK by VisitRecordLockPhrase (COBOL0900), an AT END phrase and FROM after the phrases by the parser. Two things the 1985 format does not print compile at 85. (1) The word RECORD after record-name-1: rewriteStatement is REWRITE (recordName | FILE fileName) RECORD? and no pass asks the edition, so REWRITE IDX-REC RECORD FROM WS-REC compiles; the word comes from the later format (§2002:14.8.33.1 and §2023:14.9.35.2 print RECORD, not underlined, after the braces), and the 1985 format has no such word (WRITE at 85 refuses the same word, COBOL2269). (2) The phrase order: the conditionalPhrases loop and ConditionalPhraseAssociation.Associates / MayAssociate have no edition arm for the sequence, so NOT INVALID KEY before INVALID KEY compiles; either order is the 2002 change §2002:F.2 item 33 ("The conditional phrases in the ... REWRITE ... statements may be specified in any order"), named by the row's change record. (2) is the mechanism of the DELETE, READ, START and WRITE rows of this slice. The witness runs the printed format only (FROM, both phrases in order, END-REWRITE, a present and an absent key).

next.reason: 1985: "REWRITE record-name-1 [ FROM identifier-1 ] [ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1 ] [ NOT INVALID KEY ... ]"; 2023: "FILE file-name-1 ... FROM literal-1 ... [ retry-phrase ] WITH LOCK / WITH NO LOCK; INVALID KEY group in choice indicators". 2023 format adds FILE file-name-1, FROM literal-1, the RETRY and LOCK phrases, and allows INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY in either order, so it accepts programs 1985 refused.
